- **A transparent model agrees with coaches' votes 42% more than disposals alone** (NDCG@5 0.825 vs 0.580; validation seasons; used for model selection; relative gain 95% CI +38% to +47%; Holm-adjusted p <0.001). It also beats the fantasy-points formula by +0.174 NDCG@5 (95% CI [+0.156, +0.190]).
- **The heavier model adds +0.025 NDCG@5 over the interpretable one** (95% CI [+0.016, +0.035], above the 0.01 threshold) - meeting the pre-specified statistical decision rule; practical value still needs coach review.
- **Role residuals (validation seasons):** the largest positive M1 residual is for **Midfielder** (mean +0.16 votes per player-match, 95% CI [+0.10, +0.22]); largest negative residual: Ruck (-0.20, CI [-0.30, -0.10]). Pre-registered H2a (defenders under-rated): not supported (mean residual +0.009, 95% CI [-0.018, +0.037]). Role comparisons beyond H2a are exploratory. This proxy cannot isolate unrecorded work, and non-support does not establish that a blind spot is absent (see Limitations).

Training seasons: [2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023]; validation seasons: [2024, 2025]. Effective start: 2012. Training matches: 2338; validation matches: 414.

## Test: 2026 held-out season (single run, frozen protocol)

Evaluated on 206 matches and 9476 player-matches. Frozen specifications were refitted on seasons [2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025]; no test-based model or parameter selection followed. 95% match-bootstrap intervals use 2000 resamples and paired sign-flip tests use 20000 permutations, with Holm correction across the three pre-specified contrasts within each metric. Intervals condition on the fitted models, treat matches as resampling units and do not measure uncertainty across future seasons or training runs.

- **A transparent model agrees with coaches' votes 41% more than disposals alone** (NDCG@5 0.840 vs 0.594; 2026 held-out season; relative gain 95% CI +35% to +48%; Holm-adjusted p <0.001). It also beats the fantasy-points formula by +0.172 NDCG@5 (95% CI [+0.147, +0.195]).
- **The heavier model is statistically better, but the gain is not established above the threshold:** +0.020 NDCG@5 (95% CI [+0.007, +0.032]) vs the pre-specified 0.01 threshold; the lower confidence bound does not clear it.
- **M2 minus M1, secondary findings:** Top-1 hit -0.005 [-0.063, 0.049], Holm p 1.000 (positive difference not established); Normalized Recall@5 0.025 [0.007, 0.045], Holm p 0.015 (positive difference supported); Spearman 0.026 [-0.006, 0.057], Holm p 0.095 (positive difference not established).

A failed decision rule does not establish that the gain is below delta, nor that the models are equivalent. ECE intervals are descriptive; no paired calibration test was pre-specified. This is one held-out season and measures agreement with coaches, not causal value or demonstrated usefulness to a club. Q2/Q3 below use development data only.

### Test data quality and exclusions

Included 206/207 source matches (99.517%); vote-row match rate 99.926%, vote-mass match rate 99.839%. All frozen QA gates passed. One Round 9 Sydney–Melbourne match was excluded for an unmatched vote row: the AFLCA player name includes a junior suffix absent from the AFL Tables surname, so neither frozen exact nor initial-name keys match. No test-informed alias or join change was made. Exclusion may introduce selection bias; inference covers the 206 retained matches.

## Q3 trends: features whose block CIs clearly separate

Across 23 features, 12 meet the any-pair interval criterion; 6 first-versus-last Holm tests have p < 0.05. Among the 5 pre-named features, 0 first-versus-last Holm tests meet that threshold.

The selected M1 specification is fitted separately in each season block, with one shared development-data scaler. The protocol flags any pair of non-overlapping block intervals; the Holm p-values below test first versus last blocks across features. These are different criteria. Coefficient shifts are associations on a logit scale and may reflect changing residual noise, correlated statistics, rules or model fit, rather than changed coaching preferences.

## Limits of this validation evidence

M1/M2 were selected on these same validation seasons; their reported performance and conditional confidence intervals omit model-selection uncertainty. They are not held-out estimates. Held-out results, when present, are reported separately above. Coaches' votes are subjective, public box scores omit tracking and off-ball work, and the role proxy can let the model absorb an omitted-work premium. Failure to support H2a therefore does not show that no blind spot exists. The delta = 0.01 decision threshold is a research convention, not demonstrated usefulness to a coach. 2020 had shortened quarters; statistical scaling cannot remove all season differences. No causal or adoption claim follows from these results.
